Add a new blocking CI lint, scripts/ci/checks/check_evaluator_version_bump.py, modeled on check_script_skill_sync.py's diff-aware pattern: fails when a changed content_eval/evaluators/{name}.py has no corresponding EVALUATOR_VERSIONS/EVALUATOR_LOGIC_VERSION bump in the same diff, with a narrow self-documenting exemption comment for cosmetic-only edits.
why_it_matters: Zero-blast-radius, zero-dependency fix that closes a real process gap (evaluator logic changed silently, 3 times, with no staleness signal) independent of the larger grading-visibility redesign's timeline -- see governing plan section R.3.9/R.1 point 3.

title: Codify the manual SAFE_FOR_MECHANICAL_MIGRATION/COLLISION_RISK classification into a real, tested function
objective: Build scripts/pipeline/lib/install_collision_classifier.py, codifying reports/audit/st-054-collision-classification-2026-08-16.md's own manual method (extract real namespace/using (net), import (python), ES-module import/require (typescript), quoted import path (go) tokens from runs/.clone_cache/{repo}; normalize via casefold + strip-non-alphanumeric; compare against the registry candidate) into classify_collision_risk(family, platform) -> SAFE_FOR_MECHANICAL_MIGRATION | COLLISION_RISK_STRUCTURAL | COLLISION_RISK_PENDING_VERIFICATION (fail-closed on any parse/extraction error -- never defaults to SAFE). Structural-risk is real only when the install-command token shape and the source language's own identifier shape share the same naming convention (confirmed: only NuGet+C# dotted-PascalCase, i.e. only nuget-registry-type products); pypi/npm/go_modules naming-convention differences are not real corruption risk since the prefix-anchored install-command regex can never match inside an import/using statement regardless. Wire --respect-collision-gate (default True) into package_install_migrator.py and package_install_inline_migrator.py's run_migration(), refusing to write unless SAFE_FOR_MECHANICAL_MIGRATION or --force is passed.
why_it_matters: The only existing safety classification (18 SAFE / 9 COLLISION_RISK of 27 products) is a hand-written Markdown report never loaded or enforced by any code -- any future automated orchestration could re-introduce the exact cells/net-class identity-collision corruption risk ST-054 was built to prevent. Re-deriving the classification precisely also reclassifies 8 of the 9 flagged products as actually safe, unblocking real remaining scope. See governing plan section R.3.2/R.1 point 2.
acceptance_checks: Golden-file regression test pins all 27 real products against fixture clone-cache snippets, reproducing exactly: 26 SAFE_FOR_MECHANICAL_MIGRATION, cells/net COLLISION_RISK_STRUCTURAL
A missing/unreadable clone-cache fixture resolves to COLLISION_RISK_PENDING_VERIFICATION, never SAFE (fail-closed proof)

Both migrators refuse to write against a COLLISION_RISK_* classification without --force; --dry-run summary of any of the 8 newly-reclassified-safe products manually diffed and confirmed correct before trusting the classifier's SAFE verdict for real execution

pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_install_collision_classifier.py scripts/pipeline/tests/test_package_install_migrator.py scripts/pipeline/tests/test_package_install_inline_migrator.py -q -> all green, no regression on existing tests
rollback_or_recovery: git revert the commit. The gate defaults to blocking (fail-closed), so reverting only removes the new safety check, not any content -- no content rollback needed. If already used to gate a real migration run, the migration commits themselves roll back independently per their own one-product-per-commit convention.

title: Build the durable page-level detection/remediation state-tracking artifact
objective: Build scripts/pipeline/lib/reconciliation_store.py, modeled on taskcard_store.py's locking/append discipline (FileLock from advisory_lock.py) but batch-oriented for ~20k-file sweep runs: ReconciliationStore.append_batch(records) / .read_latest() / .read_latest_for_product(family, platform), writing newline-delimited JSON to reports/package-reconciliation/inventory.jsonl (last-occurrence-per-path wins on read). Schema per row: path, family, platform, site, locale, representation (literal|shortcode_block|shortcode_inline|shortcode_maven|mixed|none), registry_type, published, collision_classification, finding_count_literal, finding_count_install_recipe_fail, sweep_run_id, base_sha, recorded_at. Add validate_reconciliation_record() to scripts/pipeline/lib/schema_validators.py.
why_it_matters: No state currently persists between detection and remediation -- every session re-derives scope from scratch, which is the primary reason 16 completed taskcards produced only ~68 of ~6,522 fixes. This artifact is the resumable work queue future sessions and automation read instead of re-discovering scope. Deliberately placed under reports/, not data/package_registry.json -- per-page granularity cannot fit that file's per-(family,platform) shape, and this mission's own plan-repair review already flagged that observation-only fields in data/ risk daily spurious full-portfolio rebuilds once the deploy-trigger fix lands. See governing plan section R.3.1.
acceptance_checks: append_batch/read_latest/read_latest_for_product round-trip correctly on a fixture batch
last-occurrence-per-path wins semantics proven when the same path appears in two different sweep_run_id batches
concurrent-write locking proven safe (two append_batch calls from separate processes/threads never corrupt the file)
validate_reconciliation_record() rejects a malformed row (missing required field, invalid representation enum value)
pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_reconciliation_store.py -q -> all green
rollback_or_recovery: This is a new, additive, reports/-scoped artifact with no consumers yet in this taskcard -- git revert the commit; no data/content rollback needed since nothing else depends on it until PKGINSTALL-CHANGE-BUDGET/PKGINSTALL-LOCALE-PATCH-MODULE/PKGINSTALL-BLOCK-UPDATER-CALLSITE/PKGINSTALL-CONTENT-HEALING-STATUS-WRITEBACK/PKGINSTALL-DEFECT-SWEEP-REDESIGN land.

title: Content-level blast-radius circuit breaker for install-instruction changes
objective: Build scripts/pipeline/lib/install_change_budget.py + scripts/pipeline/config/install_change_budgets.yaml, modeled directly on the real, working scripts/seo/pipeline/change_budget.py pattern (static caps always active + rolling-baseline anomaly check per mechanism with an explicit, always-logged warm-up period, fail-closed, never truncate-and-continue). History co-located under reports/package-reconciliation/change_budget_history.json. Each integration site (the migrators, the future locale_patch.py) builds its own proposed-change-volume object and calls check_budget() before writing.
why_it_matters: Nothing today caps or validates the blast radius of a proposed content change before it's applied -- the 'one product per commit, never one all-products commit' rule is prose-only guidance, not machine-enforced. This directly satisfies PKGINSTALL-PERMANENT-RECONCILIATION-LOOP's own stated acceptance check ('a fixture proposal set that exceeds the threshold aborts-and-defers'). See governing plan section R.3.6.
acceptance_checks: check_budget() rejects a proposed volume exceeding a static cap, fail-closed (no partial application)
warm-up mode (fewer than warmup_runs of history) always logs its INACTIVE status visibly rather than silently skipping the anomaly check
rolling-baseline anomaly check rejects a run whose proposed total exceeds anomaly_multiplier times the mean of recent actual run totals
pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_install_change_budget.py -q -> all green, mirroring change_budget.py's own existing test shapes
rollback_or_recovery: git revert the commit. Fail-closed by design -- removing this check only removes a safety gate, does not itself require any content/data rollback.

title: Build a real, tested, committed S-75 locale-propagation module
objective: Build scripts/pipeline/commands/content/locale_patch.py, generalizing S-75's exact algorithm (skills/locale-patch.md: byte-identical old_text/new_text match-or-skip, never fuzzy -- unchanged core safety principle) as a real module with its own test file, replacing the ad hoc throwaway script ST-054 TC-07 used and deleted. New capability: is_english_source_ready(family, platform, source_path) consults the reconciliation store -- refuses to propagate from an English source still representation:literal or with an unresolved COLLISION_RISK_STRUCTURAL classification. skills/locale-patch.md becomes a thin wrapper with a CONTRACT comment pointing at this module.
why_it_matters: S-75 currently has no reusable, tested, repo-committed implementation -- every future use requires re-deriving the same throwaway script from scratch, and there is no tooling today that checks English-source readiness before propagating (the skill's own docstring explicitly disclaims this as 'not this skill's responsibility'). See governing plan section R.3.5.

is_english_source_ready() refuses when the reconciliation store shows representation:literal or an unresolved COLLISION_RISK_STRUCTURAL row for the source file
run_locale_patch() calls install_change_budget.check_budget() before writing and aborts on a budget violation
skills/locale-patch.md carries a CONTRACT comment pointing at locale_patch.py and passes the existing skill-script-sync drift check
pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_locale_patch.py -q -> all green

title: Narrow the literal-mention detection regex to drop non-Aspose noise (validate before landing)
objective: In scripts/pipeline/audit/package_install_literal.py's verify_package_install_literals(), suppress a structural _INSTALL_CMD_RE match only when the captured token neither contains 'aspose' (case-insensitive) nor is empty/flag-shaped (starts with '-', e.g. '-r requirements.txt', '--upgrade'). Do NOT require exact candidate-identity match -- stay identity-agnostic for anything plausibly Aspose-related, since a hand-typed WRONG Aspose package name is exactly the defect class this gate must keep catching (3D-NET-REFRESH-002 precedent). This is explicitly a lower-confidence item: before landing, run the narrowed rule against a real snapshot of the current ~6,454 findings, manually spot-check a sample (50-100) of everything that disappears to confirm each is genuinely unrelated, and pin regression fixtures for both true positives (cells/net's real collision, the 3D-NET-REFRESH-002 shape) and the named false positives.
why_it_matters: The current regex is deliberately identity-agnostic (correct, by design) but as a side effect matches many commands with zero connection to any Aspose package (pip install -r requirements.txt, pip install --upgrade, pip install fastmcp, pip install markitdown-aspose-cells-plugin) -- 'zero findings' is not a well-defined, achievable target until this noise is characterized and removed. See governing plan section R.3.7/R.1 point 5. Confidence on the exact effect size is explicitly low until validated -- this card's own acceptance checks require that validation before merge, not after.
acceptance_checks: Regression fixtures pin known true positives (cells/net Aspose.Cells_FOSS-shaped, 3D-NET-REFRESH-002-shaped) as still-flagged after the change
Regression fixtures pin the named false positives (-r requirements.txt, --upgrade, unrelated pip install pytest) as no-longer-flagged after the change

A before/after finding-count delta run against real current content is manually spot-checked (sample of 50-100 newly-dropped findings) and the reviewed delta is published in the reconciliation store / sweep report, not silently absorbed
pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_package_install_literal.py -q -> all green
rollback_or_recovery: git revert the regex change -- this is a read-only detector, reverting it only changes what future sweeps report, no content/data rollback needed.

Every row from both sweeps is appended into ReconciliationStore.append_batch(). Rename the workflow install-literal-sweep.yml -> install-defect-sweep.yml: run the combined sweep, commit the durable report via git_plumb_commit.py (reports-only, low blast radius) instead of leaving it in the ephemeral runner, and invoke check_package_content_healing_staleness.py (real, tested, currently wired into nothing) on the same schedule. Fix the dedup gap with scripts/pipeline/commands/ops/sync_tracked_issues.py, keyed by (family, platform, defect_class) -- update/close an existing tracked issue via a stable label instead of creating a new one every run; gh issue create only when none exists for that key.

title: Close the grading-invisibility gap for install_recipe's two safety-critical checks
objective: Split install_recipe.py's shared category='IR' so _verify_publish_channel_claims gets 'IR_PUBLISH_CLAIM' and _verify_no_unpublished_disclosure gets 'IR_UNPUBLISHED_DISCLOSURE' (leave _verify_install_accuracy's 'IR' unchanged). Add SAFETY_OVERRIDE_FINDINGS: frozenset[tuple[str,str]] to content_eval/config.py covering exactly those two (evaluator, category) pairs. In content_eval/models.py, replace the inline 'f.evaluator in CANONICAL_EVALUATORS' filters in both grade_reasons() (line ~304) and compute_grade_with_criticality() (line ~414) with a shared _is_grade_eligible(f) helper: true if canonical, OR if f.level=='FAIL' and (f.evaluator, f.category) in SAFETY_OVERRIDE_FINDINGS. Add both new categories to grade_config.yaml's critical_categories. Write a new GRADE_CONTRACT.md section 10 ('Safety-Override Findings') documenting this as a lighter process than full graduation (FAIL-only, deterministic, already-tested, documented safety justification, maintainer sign-off, contract version bump -- explicitly no 14-day wait or corpus-wide noise-rate run, since those bars are about an evaluator's overall noise profile, not two already-verified FAIL-only checks). Bump EVALUATOR_LOGIC_VERSION/EVALUATOR_FREEZE_VERSION, run a full --skip-graded corpus re-evaluation, and record the resulting grade-distribution shift before merging. Ship scripts/ci/checks/check_install_recipe_safety_fails.py (hard-blocking on PR-touched files, independent of stored grade) as an immediate stopgap while this taskcard's larger change is in review; retire it once the change lands.
why_it_matters: install_recipe has been EXPERIMENTAL (never CANONICAL) since 2026-04-24, four months before the safety-critical _verify_publish_channel_claims check was written into it on 2026-08-14 -- content_eval/models.py filters every install_recipe finding out of grade computation before any category/criticality logic runs, confirmed by direct code read, so 89 real FAIL findings never surfaced despite pages grading A. Full graduation is explicitly rejected as too broad (carries unvetted WARN noise from _verify_install_accuracy) and too slow (14-day+corpus-validation process) for what's actually needed. This is this redesign's single most novel mechanism and needs maintainer sign-off on the lighter process itself, not just the code -- see governing plan section R.3.3/R.7's own honesty note that the GRADE_CONTRACT.md wording is a proposal, not a settled agreement.
acceptance_checks: A fixture page with a FAIL in IR_PUBLISH_CLAIM computes grade F via compute_grade_with_criticality() and grade_reasons() cites the critical-category override -- proving the fix actually changes grade output, not just category labels
A fixture page with a FAIL in the untouched, non-safety IR category (_verify_install_accuracy) does NOT flip grade -- proving the override is narrowly scoped, not a blanket install_recipe graduation
GRADE_CONTRACT.md section 10 is written and the contract version is bumped per its own section 9 rules
A full --skip-graded corpus re-evaluation is run and its grade-distribution shift (before/after counts per grade letter) is recorded in evidence_refs before this card can close
check_install_recipe_safety_fails.py hard-blocks a PR touching a file with either safety FAIL, independent of that file's stored grade

pytest scripts/pipeline/tests/test_install_recipe.py scripts/pipeline/tests/content_eval/test_models.py scripts/pipeline/tests/test_check_install_recipe_safety_fails.py -q -> all green, full test suite shows no new failures vs. the ST-054 TC-10 baseline
rollback_or_recovery: git revert the commit(s). Since this changes grade computation portfolio-wide, revert must be followed by a second --skip-graded corpus re-evaluation to confirm grades return to their pre-change distribution -- a revert here is not zero-cost, unlike most other cards in this batch.
